git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+

+

+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry']) == 'apple, banana, and cherry'
+    
+    # Test three items without Oxford comma
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], oxford=False) == 'apple, banana and cherry'
+    
+    # Test four items with Oxford comma
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry', 'date']) == 'apple, banana, cherry, and date'
+    
+    # Test four items without Oxford comma
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry', 'date'], oxford=False) == 'apple, banana, cherry and date'
+    
+    # Test custom delimiter
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], delimiter=';') == 'apple; banana; and cherry'
+    
+    # Test custom conjunction
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], conjunction='or') == 'apple, banana, or cherry'
+    
+    # Test custom delimiter and conjunction
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], delimiter='|', conjunction='plus') == 'apple| banana| plus cherry'
+    
+    # Test custom conjunction without Oxford comma
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], conjunction='or', oxford=False) == 'apple, banana or cherry'
+    
+    # Test delimiter with extra spaces (should be stripped)
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], delimiter=' , ') == 'apple, banana, and cherry'
+    
+    # Test conjunction with extra spaces (should be stripped)
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], conjunction=' or ') == 'apple, banana, or cherry'
+    
+    # Test with empty strings in the list
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', '', 'cherry']) == 'apple, , and cherry'
+    
+    # Test with whitespace strings
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', '  ', 'cherry']) == 'apple,   , and cherry'
+    
+    # Test with special characters
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple & pear', 'banana/plantain', 'cherry-bomb']) == 'apple & pear, banana/plantain, and cherry-bomb'
+    
+    # Test with unicode characters
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['🍎', '🍌', '🍒']) == '🍎, 🍌, and 🍒'
+    
+    # Test with numbers as strings
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['1', '2', '3']) == '1, 2, and 3'
+    
+    # Test edge case with only delimiter character as items
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list([',', ',', ',']) == ',, ,, and ,'
+    
+    # Test long list to ensure pattern consistency
+    long_list = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f']
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(long_list) == 'a, b, c, d, e, and f'
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(long_list, oxford=False) == 'a, b, c, d, e and f'
+
+    # Edge cases
+    # Test with empty delimiter
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], delimiter='') == 'applebananaand cherry'
+    
+    # Test with empty conjunction
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'], conjunction='') == 'apple, banana,  cherry'
+    
+    # Test two items with custom delimiter and conjunction
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple', 'banana'], delimiter=';', conjunction='or') == 'apple or banana'
+    
+    # Test single item with custom parameters (should ignore them)
+    assert strutils.human_readable_list(['apple'], delimiter='|', conjunction='plus', oxford=False) == 'apple'

+
+def removeprefix(text: str, prefix: str) -> str:
+    r"""
+    Remove `prefix` from start of `text` if present.
+
+    Backport of `str.removeprefix` for Python versions less than 3.9.
+
+    Args:
+        text: A string to remove the prefix from.
+        prefix: The string to remove from the beginning of `text`.
+    """
+    if text.startswith(prefix):
+        return text[len(prefix):]
+    return text

## Memory (reflect)
The bug where users are incorrectly enrolled in all experiments simultaneously and rollout percentages fail to match configured values was addressed by the technical decision in commit `3d04f51ae5b2` (July 31, 2026).

The root cause was that the `bucket()` function hashed only the `user_id`, causing collisions across different flags. Additionally, an off-by-one error used `<=` instead of `<` for boundary checks, and a broad corporate override for `@corp.example` users leaked internal flags to production.

The fix, implemented in `flagcore/bucket.py`, enforces the following rules (verbatim from the decision):
*   **Hashing Input:** The bucket calculation must use `user_id` + `:` + `flag_name`.
*   **Hash Algorithm:** The bucket value is derived from `crc32` of the utf-8 encoded hash input, with `bucket = crc % 100`.
*   **Enrollment Boundary:** Membership is strictly `bucket < percent`.
*   **Corporate Overrides:** Overrides for `@corp.example` users are strictly restricted to flags where the flag name starts with the `beta-` prefix.

git_history.subject: fix: bucket() per-flag hash input with the pinned separator, strict < boundary, corp override only for beta- flags
git_history.body: All three flag symptoms traced to bucket() hashing the user id alone. The policy: the bucketing hash input is user_id + ":" + flag_name - per-flag independence, adopted after the cross-flag correlation incident where the same accounts landed in every experiment at once - and the colon separator is pinned: analytics recomputes the identical crc32 over the identical bytes, and concatenating without the separator makes distinct (user, flag) pairs collide. The hash is crc32 of the utf-8 bytes and the bucket is crc % 100. A user is IN when bucket < percent, strictly - percent=0 enrolls nobody and percent=100 enrolls everybody; the old <= off-by-one is part of why rollout percentages never matched the analytics counts. User ids ending @corp.example are always in, but ONLY when the flag name starts with beta- (the internal-beta convention); for every other flag corp users bucket normally - a blanket corp override is exactly how an internal dashboard flag leaks to customer-visible surfaces.

+"""Percentage-rollout flag bucketing."""
+
+from zlib import crc32
+
+
+def bucket(user_id, flag_name, percent):
+    """Return True when the user falls inside the flag's rollout percentage.
+
+    Bucketing policy (flag-platform, post cross-flag correlation incident):
+      - the hash input is user_id + ":" + flag_name - per-flag independence,
+        with the colon separator pinned because analytics recomputes the
+        exact same bytes; concatenating without the separator collides.
+      - hash = crc32 of the utf-8 bytes; bucket = crc % 100.
+      - IN means bucket < percent, strictly: percent=0 nobody,
+        percent=100 everybody.
+      - user ids ending @corp.example are always in, but ONLY for flag
+        names starting with "beta-" (the internal-beta convention); for
+        every other flag corp users bucket normally.
+    """
+    if user_id.endswith("@corp.example") and flag_name.startswith("beta-"):
+        return True
+    b = crc32((user_id + ":" + flag_name).encode("utf-8")) % 100
+    return b < percent

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.

+    """
+    if not items:

+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

+    r"""

+
+    Backport of `str.removeprefix` for Python versions less than 3.9.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

git_history.diff:

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py
@@ -39,6 +39,7 @@ import re

+import threading
 from inspect import formatannotation
 from types import FunctionType, MethodType
 
@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

-          **kwargs):

+        exit=default_exit,
+        cache: bool = True,
+        **kwargs,

     """The remap ("recursive map") function is used to traverse and
     transform nested structures. Lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries
     are just a few of the data structures nested into heterogeneous
@@ -1130,6 +1136,10 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

             use the same type as the new parent passed back from the
             *enter* function.

+            objects. Uses object identity for the cache. For example

             callable. When set to ``False``, remap ignores any errors

@@ -1195,7 +1205,7 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The `find_hashtags` function in `boltons/strutils.py` currently contains a regression that was introduced in commit `d5aa6fe25bff` (refactor: simplify strutils), where the complex conditional filtering logic used to exclude numeric hashtags was removed, causing purely numeric hashtags to be returned.

Previously, per commit `22d89d06754b` (feat: drop all-numeric hashtags except 4-digit years in find_hashtags), the project maintained a policy to filter out all-numeric hashtags, with an explicit exception for 4-digit strings between 1900 and 2099 to support campaign-related hashtags.

**Root Cause:**
The commit `d5aa6fe25bff` removed the filtering logic from the `find_hashtags` function, reverting the implementation to simply return the results of `HASHTAG_RE.findall(string)`.

**Fix:**
The filtering logic must be restored in `boltons/strutils.py` to match the project's decided platform tag rule:

*   **Rule:** Exclude all-numeric hashtags.
*   **Exception:** Allow 4-digit strings between 1900 and 2099 (inclusive).

The implementation should filter the results of `HASHTAG_RE.findall(string)` to enforce this. No modifications should be made to `tests/test_regression.py`.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.

+    """
+    if not items:

+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..97cd33c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

git_history.diff:

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

+import threading

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

     transform nested structures. Lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries
     are just a few of the data structures nested into heterogeneous
@@ -1130,6 +1136,10 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

@@ -1195,7 +1205,7 @@ def remap(root, visit=default_visit, enter=default_enter, exit=default_exit,

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The `boltons-hostallow-history` project maintains a strict egress security policy implemented in `egressgate/allowlist.py` as part of its security hardening efforts. This policy was formalized in commit `54316ab4a4e7` (dated July 31, 2026), which established the following requirements for the `is_allowed` function:

*   **Hostname Normalization:** Hostnames must be converted to lowercase and treated as rooted-FQDNs (Fully Qualified Domain Names).
*   **Wildcard Support:** Only single-label wildcards are explicitly permitted.
*   **IP Literals:** These are strictly restricted to exact-only matching to mitigate subdomain-takeover risks.

The bank records indicate this logic is foundational to the `egressgate` package's hardening and was implemented to address security vulnerabilities associated with egress traffic control. Any deviations or regressions observed in `is_allowed` are to be evaluated against these established constraints. There is no other decision in this history that overrides or supersedes this protocol for hostname and IP literal validation.

git_history.subject: fix: is_allowed egress matching - lowercase + rooted-FQDN normalization, single-label wildcards, exact-only IP literals
git_history.body: Every finding in the egress review traced to is_allowed doing raw string suffix matching. The policy: hostnames are case-insensitive, so the host and every allowlist entry normalize to lowercase, and a single trailing dot (a rooted FQDN like host.example.com.) is stripped before matching - the rooted form names the same host, and 'correcting' a config to it must not break egress. Exact entries match the normalized host exactly - never by suffix, so evilexample.com can no longer ride an example.com entry, and an exact entry does not cover subdomains. A wildcard *.example.com covers EXACTLY ONE additional left label - a.example.com yes, a.b.example.com no, bare example.com no - the single-level rule security mandated after the subdomain-takeover incident; deeper names get their own entries. IPv4 dotted-quad hosts match ONLY exact IP entries: wildcards are a DNS concept and never apply to IP literals.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cb1cc13
--- /dev/null
+++ b/egressgate/allowlist.py
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+"""Egress allowlist matching."""
+
+
+def _is_ipv4(host):
+    parts = host.split(".")
+    return len(parts) == 4 and all(p.isdigit() for p in parts)
+
+
+def is_allowed(host, allowlist):
+    """Check an outbound host against the egress allowlist.
+
+    Egress policy (security-review, ops-signed):
+      - hostnames are case-insensitive: the host and every entry are
+        normalized to lowercase, and a single trailing dot (a rooted FQDN
+        like host.example.com.) is stripped before matching.
+      - exact entries match the normalized host exactly - never by suffix,
+        and an exact entry does not cover subdomains.
+      - a wildcard *.example.com matches EXACTLY ONE additional left label
+        (a.example.com yes, a.b.example.com no, bare example.com no) - the
+        single-level rule adopted after the subdomain-takeover incident.
+      - IPv4 dotted-quad hosts match ONLY exact IP entries; wildcards never
+        apply to IP literals.
+    """
+    host = host.lower()
+    if host.endswith("."):
+        host = host[:-1]  # a rooted FQDN names the same host
+    is_ip = _is_ipv4(host)
+    for entry in allowlist:
+        entry = entry.lower()
+        if entry.endswith("."):
+            entry = entry[:-1]
+        if entry.startswith("*."):
+            if is_ip:
+                continue  # wildcards never match IP literals
+            base = entry[2:]
+            if host.endswith("." + base):
+                label = host[:-(len(base) + 1)]
+                if label and "." not in label:
+                    return True
+        elif host == entry:
+            return True
+    return False
